findings.reason: as written the only compliant placement puts prose about a different quantity into every sibling's documentation, so the node cannot satisfy the section's own purpose without a token-keyed placement mechanism (or an explicit family-wide scope) that the plan does not name.
findings.text: §5 places each sentence "in the documentation of the template that renders the unqualified or total quantity", but a template is keyed by base plus segment kinds and selected by subset match (`grammar/terms.py:297-306`), so a whole pattern shares it: at HEAD `cba614f`, `select_conventions` returns `temperature/[subject]` for `electron_temperature`, `neutral_temperature` and `cold_neutral_temperature` alike, `density/[subject]` for `total_electron_density`, `fast_electron_density` and `thermal_electron_density`, and the bare `triangularity` template for both `triangularity_of_plasma_boundary` and `upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary` — so the neutral-population sentence would render into `electron_temperature`'s documentation and the "unqualified triangularity" sentence onto `upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary`; the plan's own done-when renders one name per ruling and so cannot see the leak

findings.reason: the plan names the ruling field as the wording authority, so a builder that opens the JSON gets the right text; only a builder copying the visible list would inherit the truncation, and tightening the claim costs one edit rather than redirecting a node.
findings.text: §5 states "The exact wording is each ruling's `template_sentence`" while quoting three shortened variants beside it (`"Total density is the sum of the thermal and fast populations."` for the field's `"…populations of the species; thermal excludes the suprathermal particles that fast names."`, and the first clause only for the triangularity ruling)
